classification.difficultyReason: Establish equal directed opposite sides and apply the parallelogram test.

content.prompt:
The quadrilateral $ABCD$ has vertices $A(-7,-5)$, $B(8,-2)$, $C(10,9)$ and $D(-5,6)$.

Show that $\overrightarrow{AD}=\overrightarrow{BC}$, and hence explain why $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.

answer.short: $\overrightarrow{AD}=\overrightarrow{BC}=\begin{pmatrix}2\\11\end{pmatrix}$. One pair of opposite sides is equal and parallel, so $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AD}&=\overrightarrow{OD}-\overrightarrow{OA}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}-5-(-7)\\6-(-5)\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}2\\11\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{BC}&=\overrightarrow{OC}-\overrightarrow{OB}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}10-8\\9-(-2)\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}2\\11\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}$$
Hence $\overrightarrow{AD}=\overrightarrow{BC}$. Therefore $ABCD$ is a parallelogram, since one pair of opposite sides is equal in length and parallel.
